summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch ran a chapter of John L. Sullivan's memoir arguing he was the true world champion, with a list of past title fights that included Tom Allen's bouts with McCoole, Mace, Hogan and Goss.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'Saturday Evening, January 22, 1910. St. Louis Post-Dispatch', page 8, Live Sporting News and Comment.

facts.fact: Sullivan's 1910 memoir listed McCoole as beating Allen in 1869 for the championship of the world
Sullivan's memoir listed Jem Mace beating Allen in 1870 for the title and $5,000 at 'Keanville' (Kennerville), near New Orleans
Allen beat McCoole on Sept. 23, 1873, at Chouteau Island near St. Louis, according to Sullivan's memoir
Ben Hogan fought Allen on Nov. 18, 1873, for $2,000 and the championship of the Pacific coast; Allen was winning when a wrangle broke up the fight, per Sullivan's memoir
Joe Goss fought Allen on Sept. 7, 1876, in Kentucky for $2,000 and the championship of the world; Goss was declared winner, per Sullivan's memoir

notes: A secondhand retrospective by Sullivan; the Allen fights are a few lines in a longer list of champions. The current summary does not mention Allen.
